feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/communications leadership. It is generally well written and polished, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, fewer repeated skill sections, and more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility and scale signals: examples like a 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and analytics stack modernization add substance.  
- Writing is concise and professional overall, with strong domain vocabulary and no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve readability and make the CV feel sharper.  
- Add more measurable impact: several bullets describe responsibilities (“led,” “advised,” “developed”) without showing results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, or campaign outcomes.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists varies; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” would read more cleanly as “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add a scale cue from recent experience to increase impact, e.g., “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Tighten the list of focus areas so it feels less exhaustive and more strategic.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers enterprise platforms and editorial systems that support complex, mission-driven organizations, including 10,000+ page web ecosystems, multi-team publishing models, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled content discovery.”
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” overlaps heavily with the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on higher-value differentiators.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable phrases with consistent noun structure; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “experiences” unevenly.
- Prioritize the strongest, most current differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation/integrations, and multimedia.
- Consider replacing “Advocacy and public-sector communications” with “Public-sector digital communications” for cleaner phrasing and broader relevance.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Public-sector digital communications • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is also repeated elsewhere; keep only if targeting advocacy-focused roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the footer more selective will improve impact and reduce redundancy.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and purpose.
- Use parallel, outcome-oriented phrasing: “Led/Developed/Built…” + tool/scope + result.
- Tighten wording and remove filler: e.g., “bill-level AI chat” is strong; “designed for continued campaign growth” could become “built for reuse and expansion.”
- Consider this rewrite:  
  **Selected Recent Projects**  
  **AI Hybrid Search** — Led development of an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery.  
  **We Are Counties Microsite** — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources in a reusable modular architecture.  
  **Organization Anniversary Campaign** — Delivered a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display.  
  **Advocacy Video Series** — Produced an ongoing advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search, microsite work, and advocacy video already appear in recent NACo roles; this footer should stay concise and project-focused rather than restating responsibilities.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical breadth, but it reads too much like a services list. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scope where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise the National Association of Counties on enterprise digital strategy, communications operations and web modernization for large public-facing platforms.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance: emphasize what changed, e.g., “Redesigned cross-channel workflows, analytics and governance to improve coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work outcome-focused: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components and member toolkits to support advocacy and engagement initiatives.”
- Recast the AI/search bullet as a flagship achievement: “Lead AI-enabled search initiative, defining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording overlaps with the footer project list; keep this entry at the leadership/outcomes level and let “Recent Projects” hold specific builds.
- Avoid repeating governance/analytics/platform modernization language already covered in the 2022–2024 Director role unless you show new consultant-level scope or results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the biggest achievement and compress supporting detail: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email/social growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Combine infrastructure/operations bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and expanded analytics/reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening decision-making, publishing standards, and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this one focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program expansion also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize the studio build and organizational capability shift here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads more like support work than a step-up in leadership. Tighten it around scope, repeatable channels, and systems/process impact.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Managed day-to-day multi-channel digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and emphasize ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show program-building: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more outcome-oriented: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.” If possible, add metrics such as send volume, production cadence, turnaround time, or audience growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version focused on execution/operations, not enterprise leadership.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; here, stress expansion/scaling rather than initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered advocacy and member communications
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for something more differentiated, such as “Content governance and publishing standards” or “Cross-functional editorial planning.”
- If space allows, align wording to proven outcomes from recent roles, e.g., “enterprise web modernization” or “communications systems leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. For a topline section, emphasize highest-value, recent strengths and group lower-priority tools more cleanly.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; they read as secondary versus recent Drupal-led modernization work.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, use “enterprise CMS modernization” instead of “CMS modernization” to better match the scale shown in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content; keep it here only if you trim it elsewhere.
- Tool lists here substantially overlap with Technical + IT; this section should stay more strategic and selective.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, emphasize strategic analytics capability over listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, outcomes-oriented mix of tools + leadership value:
- **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership reporting • SEO, performance and conversion analysis**
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” for more standard phrasing.
- If space allows, add one higher-value capability such as “analytics infrastructure” or “measurement strategy” to better reflect recent director-level work.
- Keep the strongest, most recent tools only; this section should signal scope, not repeat the full stack.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; use Topline Skills for strategic framing and leave the fuller tool list below.
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; avoid repeating both verbatim.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and aligned to recent leadership-level multimedia work, not just production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward scope and delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production and editing • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production”
- If space allows, add a leadership cue: “Multimedia production leadership” or “Studio and event production leadership” instead of just “Video production.”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools, formats, and functions unevenly.
- If you want stronger impact, tie to recent work: “Broadcast-quality studio production” better reflects the in-house studio built in the 2022–2024 role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- Tool-level detail like PTZ may be too granular here since Technical + IT already carries execution detail.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add context on level of use or be trimmed to emphasize the most relevant platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, proven platforms: lead with Drupal and SharePoint/Power Pages only if they reflect meaningful hands-on use.
- Replace the flat list with a tighter version such as: “Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migration support) • WordPress • SharePoint / Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency framing rather than more tools: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; lightweight publishing: GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it was only used for simple static sites and not central to recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus broader capabilities.
- “CMS modernization” in Topline Skills already conveys platform breadth; avoid repeating identical platform names in both places unless this section adds specificity.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools, not basic coding labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add level/context instead of just tools, e.g. **Front-end implementation for Drupal/WordPress, tag deployment, serverless scripting, CI/CD automation**
- If space allows, swap one generic term for an outcome-oriented phrase: **API-driven integrations** or **deployment automation** rather than just listing tools

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep the fuller version in one place only
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** unless this section is specifically for implementation tooling

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and prioritize true automation tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier” then “Jira • Asana” then collaboration tools.
- Remove lower-signal/general workplace apps unless they are central to delivery; suggested rewrite: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- If space allows, sharpen the label to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems” to better match the contents.
- If you have evidence from recent roles, consider adding a brief qualifier elsewhere, e.g., “built cross-team workflows and reporting automations,” rather than expanding this list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same emphasis in multiple sections.
- Basecamp and Trello may feel dated given the more senior, recent experience.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement systems leadership. Since email operations already appear in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for clarity and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If these were used hands-on in recent roles, consider adding one qualifier only if true: **enterprise email automation**, **newsletter operations**, or **member communications**
- Example rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email automation, newsletter and member engagement platforms)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent work experience.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” and email leadership are already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience, so keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show depth or specialization. Tighten it into a sharper technical stack entry and avoid generic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Put the most strategic/recent tools first: lead with GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, since those are directly reinforced by the 2022–2024 director role.
- Change vague nouns to clearer capability labels: “SEO” → “SEO analysis”; “Dashboarding” → “KPI/dashboard reporting.”
- If space allows elsewhere, quantify impact in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., analytics stack supporting a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this one tools-only.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced elsewhere in the CV; keep only if you can support it in recent experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete scope or outputs if you can add them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted through two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes/scope where possible: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If metrics exist, combine into one concise version: “Supported a major website refresh, launched recurring video/livestream production, and improved cross-channel publishing consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching or establishing the format.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; here, focus on building the initial team/process foundation.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a stronger second sentence: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes launched, audiences reached, teams supported, or research/products delivered.
- Remove filler like “contributed to” and “materials”; use direct verbs such as coordinated, produced, launched, managed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Podcast/multimedia work overlaps with later video and digital production roles; keep this entry focused on “first podcast” and innovation/research support.
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing if later roles already show larger-scale digital leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is currently generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep workflow/production capabilities in experience or topline skills.
